what: Darden Restaurants owns 2,200 full-service restaurants including Olive Garden, LongHorn Steakhouse, Cheddar's, Yard House, Ruth's Chris and The Capital Grille. Unlike most restaurant groups it owns rather than franchises them.
customers: American families and groups eating out, across casual dining and fine dining price points.
money: Ruth's Chris, The Capital Grille, Yard House, Cheddar's
moat: Purchasing scale across 2,200 restaurants, which lets it price below independent competitors while keeping margins, plus brands with decades of customer habit.
risks: Casual dining traffic falls when consumers cut discretionary spending
Beef costs have risen sharply, which hits LongHorn and the steakhouses
Labour costs rise faster than menu prices in many states
Analyst targets imply the shares are already fully valued
opportunities: Revenue grew about 9% last year with a return on invested capital of 18%
Olive Garden's delivery partnership has added sales without building restaurants
A dividend yield near 3% with consistent increases
watch: Same-restaurant sales and traffic, and beef cost inflation.
